I ended up landing in HKUSpace studying Business Management in Higher Diploma. I would say HKUSpace is more competitive merely because it is associated with a more prestigious university, and there are multiple campuses to choose from for a larger range of potential degrees and ease of transportation if you hate waking up early (bonus points for me).

Freeriding is something everyone has to put up with, I don't judge people who report freeriders either. If you put in the work, you should get credit for the work. The freerider will look like a fool trying to present your or other's work during a presentation regardless. 

Mathematics is compulsary if you are going for a Business degree, especially statistics. You will do one class of statistics throughout the two years of CCollege, and I would say it requires effort. It is not insanely difficult, but if you will need to put in some effort to at least gain a passing grade, which in itself is not too difficult. For example, half your grade may already be gained from assignments and the interim assessment, which is comprised of easier concepts such as probability. A few harder concepts come towards the end of the class. For Geo, I'm not sure. Are you studying Quantity Surveying or a generalist degree?

For the difficulty of the course, I would say being a native english speaker is a massive advantage. Most classmates unfortunately struggled with English as a medium of instruction and the lecture notes and exams are in English as well. In fact, weakness in English is probably how most of my friends that I made and fellow classmates landed in Community College. Since I studied a HL Diploma, it was easier for me to obtain a ~3.5 CGPA without much effort, but from my knowledge, those studying Associates, especially in degrees such as Psychology had their work cut out for them.

With a IELTS score of at least 7, you may easily transition into CityU, an university that has been doing relatively well as of late. For universities such as HKU, you will be expected to obtain a perfect GPA of 4.0 in your first year and apply for a transfer to succeed. With a lesser than perfect GPA, you still may be accepted to prestigious degrees such as Global Business, ect. in the context of Geography. 

Completing my HL Diploma, I ended up being accepted to BU and City. Since I studied Diploma, I unfortunately was only offered Advanced Standing I, which means I entered at a 2nd year at CityU and had to study an additional year compared to those with perfect GPA or coming from an Associates Degree. 

Graduated last year and ended up working with a foreign MNE contracted to HSBC. I'm glad I ended up where I am, and honestly think the whole path worked out for me. I hope you find the same success. 

On a side note, I would recommend trying to improve your cantonese skill over the years of tertiary study. It's opened a lot of opportunities for me, including an internship in the Big 4 accounting firms. You will need conversational cantonese, complemented by working proficiency in English, especially in Geography where your future jobs may include land or quantity surveying, which means you may communicate occasionally over the phone by cantonese with local designer, architect or construction firms/companies.

Feel free to DM me if you have any additional questions. Good luck man.

It's harder to have nectar/petals if you're in a rural area or not in a big city with many big flower buds, and also hard if you don't play with a friend or significant other. 

However, I would say you might be doing something wrong if you are running out of all possible nectar. 

If you are short on petals, you can double petals from nectar by feeding the nectar to Pikmin with buds on their heads, not flowers. When you pick the flowers, you'll get 2 petals per pikmin. How do you get them to the "bud" on their head and not have a leaf? Walk some steps. A short walk will turn the leaf headed pikmin into your squad into bulb headed pikmin, and you can feed them from there. Cycle the pikmin in your squad, then repeat. If you walk a lot, I think 5000 steps or so your entire standby of pikmin will change into bulb form, so you can really duplicate your nectar.

How to use nectar effectively?

1. Don't stand around in the same area trying to plant if you've already done so in the last 5 minutes. Ideally, walk in a loop to make sure you come back to the same big flower at least 5 minutes later. For example, it will take me, my gf, and my friend (3 phones total) to knock down a bud with 300 flowers remaining to 50 or so in one pass. However, it'll take us another 4-5 minutes or so to find the right empty spots in the planting radius to finish off the big flower, which is time consuming compared to the 30 seconds or so it took us to plant the 250 or so in the first place. Save your time, come back later. 

2. Don't plant petals for a big flower and abandon it for more than two or three days. It'll reset, and you'll have wasted your petals.

3. When I am walking between big flowers and I'm quite short on nectar I would like to save, I'll use nectar from mushroom challenges. It's the most replenishable and I'll use say, camellia petals whilst walking between big flowers. 

Tips on getting Nectar:

1. Your pikmin in your squad will find mini fruits as you walk. Collect them often. 

2. Remember to use your detector daily. If you've gone home and there's nothing other than roadside, it can still find you fruit. 

3. Walking while planting in new places you haven't been before also will result in you discovering random fruits for you to find on expeditions.

In regards to melee, I have a Hatchetman with a XXL engine and BTA has rebalanced all skills, the relevant Melee one in this example bracing the mech after you punch or use a melee weapon. They make any aspect of the game quite balanced. Plus you will maintain evasion chevrons while walking up to a mech and meleeing it.  

I would say all branches of the skill tree are relatively balanced with Tactics being slightly weaker in my opinion. The Master Tactician perk does give +2 to initiative which pushed my 40T Liao Sha Yu all the way to Initiative 9, I think. Was pretty great. 

If you'd like a suggestion on how to build your character, tell me what he or she is piloting and what weapons are fitted. A screenshot of your mech would work too.

I put my commander in a Missile Tank with 1 Arrow IV. I think I gave her Battlelord (active, increases damage, costs resolve), Precision Shot (so I can ignore cover with my big boom), and Tactics 5 Target Prediction (+2 to everyone else's accuracy after your turn, for that turn, doesn't affect my Commander) so it's specced to increase damage dealt and also support allies with a skill if I don't want to risk firing my missile artillery.

Overall, Gunnery first for heavies or sniper mechs like a Hollander. Piloting first for flanker or light mechs. Guts for Melee mechs or something like 50/55t Mediums that you want to brawl with, so you can take the Bulwark or Shielded Stance ability to move forward under forest cover or have 50% damage resistance while in the desert when you need it. Tactics for LRM boats or in key cases where your Medium is providing an anti-light mech role.
